books.title: अवसर

books.title: युद्ध

books.title: अभ्युदय
books.author: नरेन्द्र कोहली

books.concept: The Ganga at sunrise, from Narendra Kohli's Ram-katha Abhyuday: the boatman Guha, a strong, weathered tribal chief, rows a long wooden boat across the wide river; in it sit Ram and Lakshman, youthful and clean-shaven, in simple ochre bark-cloth garments with their bows, and Sita in a plain ochre cotton sari, looking back toward the shore; mist on the water, a coral sun rising.

books.title: काबुलीवाला

books.palette: deep twilight blue, indigo, warm lamp gold
books.concept: Calcutta in the 1890s, from Tagore's story Kabuliwala: Rahmat, a tall Afghan dry-fruit seller in his forties with a thick dark beard, large grey turban, long kurta, worn embroidered waistcoat and a heavy cloth sack, crouches on the worn stone steps of an old house and holds out raisins and almonds to Mini, a five-year-old Bengali girl in a cotton frock who smiles shyly; carved wooden door, peeling lime-washed walls, a lit gas lamp, narrow lane at blue hour.

books.title: क्षुधित पाषाण
books.author: रवींद्रनाथ ठाकुर
books.palette: moonlit marble white, deep emerald-black water, faded rose
books.concept: The Deccan in the 1890s, from Tagore's story Kshudhit Pashan (The Hungry Stones): late at night a young tax collector in a white kurta and dhoti stands spellbound on the moonlit marble steps of a deserted 250-year-old Mughal palace that descend into the river Susta; around him, half-seen in the river mist like a memory, faint figures of veiled women in Persian silks seem to drift down the steps; rose petals on the wet marble.

books.title: घरे-बाइरे
books.author: रवींद्रनाथ ठाकुर
books.palette: vermilion red, crimson, ember orange, deep night
books.concept: Bengal in 1905, from Tagore's novel Ghare-Baire: Bimala, a young Bengali woman in a red-bordered white silk sari with sindoor and conch-shell and red lac bangles, stands at a tall barred wooden window of an old zamindar mansion at night, her face lit by firelight, torn and uncertain; behind her in a dim lamp-lit room her husband Nikhilesh reads quietly; outside, softly out of focus, a crowd around a bonfire of foreign cloth, sparks rising.

books.title: पथेर पाँचाली
books.author: बिभूतिभूषण बंद्योपाध्याय
books.palette: silvery white kash flowers, soft grey sky, muted monsoon green, almost black-and-white
books.concept: Rural Bengal in the 1920s, from Bibhutibhushan Bandyopadhyay's novel Pather Panchali: Apu, a thin six-year-old village boy in a loose white cotton shirt, and his older sister Durga, about twelve, barefoot in a faded cotton sari, run hand in hand through a field of tall white kash flowers towards a distant steam train trailing a long plume of black smoke along the horizon; overcast monsoon sky.

books.title: श्रीकांत

books.palette: ink-black night, deep river blue, ember orange glow
books.concept: Bengal in the early 1900s, from Saratchandra Chattopadhyay's novel Srikant: at night two boys — young Srikant, wide-eyed, and his fearless older friend Indranath, a lean teenager pulling an oar — row a small wooden boat across the dark, wide Ganga; a hanging lantern lights their faces; a cremation pyre glows orange on the distant bank under a thin crescent moon.

books.title: अपने-अपने अजनबी
books.author: अज्ञेय

books.concept: A snowbound mountain cabin in Europe in deep winter, from Agyeya's novel Apne-Apne Ajnabi: inside a small whitewashed log cabin, the frail old woman Selma, white-haired and serene, sits wrapped in a wool shawl beside a small iron stove, while the young woman Yoke stands at the frosted window with her arms crossed, restless and afraid; snow piled against the glass, pale winter daylight, a single candle.

books.title: ऐ लड़की
books.author: कृष्णा सोबती
books.palette: warm cream, marigold orange, soft afternoon light
books.concept: A Delhi home in the 1990s, from Krishna Sobti's novel Ae Ladki: a bedridden old mother, frail but fiercely alive, with silver hair, thin gold bangles and a white cotton sari, lies propped on pillows on a white bed and talks with spirit to her middle-aged daughter, who sits beside her holding her hand and listening; sheer white curtains, soft afternoon light, a brass bowl of marigolds on the bedside table.

books.title: चंद्रकांता संतति
books.author: देवकीनंदन खत्री

books.concept: A hidden tilism beneath an old fort in 19th-century north India, from Devaki Nandan Khatri's Chandrakanta Santati: the young prince Indrajit Singh — handsome, with a thin moustache, in an embroidered angarkha and turban, sword in hand — and a sharp-eyed aiyyar (master spy) holding up an oil lantern discover a massive stone door carved with lotus medallions, coiled serpents and elephant reliefs (ornamental carving only, no letters or script) deep inside a torch-lit underground passage; dust hangs in the lamplight.

books.title: भूतनाथ
books.author: देवकीनंदन खत्री
books.palette: charcoal black, smoky grey, warm lantern amber
books.concept: A ruined hill fort at night in 19th-century north India, from Devaki Nandan Khatri's Bhootnath: Gadadhar Singh, the legendary aiyyar later called Bhootnath — a middle-aged man with piercing eyes, a thick moustache and a weathered face, wrapped in a dark shawl and turban — steps out of a secret tunnel in a crumbling wall, holding an oil lantern low and glancing back over his shoulder; a cloth bundle of disguises at his belt; moonlit mist over the ramparts.

books.title: काजर की कोठरी
books.author: देवकीनंदन खत्री
books.palette: kohl black, soot grey, bridal red and gold
books.concept: A zamindar's haveli in north India around 1900, from Devaki Nandan Khatri's Kajar ki Kothri: the young bride Sarla, in a red wedding sari with gold jewellery and henna on her hands, sits imprisoned in a dark, soot-blackened room lit only by a thin shaft of light from a high grille, her eyes fierce rather than afraid; through a half-open door behind her, two scheming young men in angarkhas whisper by an oil lamp.

books.title: नरेंद्र-मोहिनी
books.author: देवकीनंदन खत्री
books.palette: soft peach, rose, pearl white, warm golden light
books.concept: A princely estate in Bihar in the 1890s, from Devaki Nandan Khatri's Narendra-Mohini: the young prince Narendra, in a cream angarkha and turban, pauses on a garden path among rose bushes at golden hour, captivated; above him on a carved sandstone balcony the alluring Mohini, in a jewelled peach lehenga, leans on the railing with a knowing smile; half-hidden behind a pillar, Rambha, the gentle girl he was meant to marry, watches sadly.

books.title: वीरेंद्र वीर
books.author: देवकीनंदन खत्री
books.palette: burnished copper sunset, deep shadow, ember red
books.concept: A Rajput hill fort at sunset, from Devaki Nandan Khatri's Virendra Veer: the young warrior Virendra Singh — lean and fierce, with a thin moustache, in a quilted angarkha with a red turban sash flying in the wind — stands on a rocky cliff with his sword drawn, guarding the narrow path to the fort; below, a line of enemy soldiers with flaming torches climbs the slope, and an aiyyar in disguise watches from behind a rock.

books.title: जय यौधेय
books.author: राहुल सांकृत्यायन
books.palette: dusty bronze, pale dawn sky blue, dry grass gold
books.concept: The Yaudheya republic between the Yamuna and the Sutlej, about 350 CE, from Rahul Sankrityayan's Jai Yaudheya: at dawn on a grassy hilltop, the young Yaudheya warrior Jay — strong and sunburnt, in a simple cotton tunic, with a bronze-tipped spear and a round shield — speaks passionately to the gana assembly of elders and armed citizens, men and women seated in a circle on stones; a tribal banner flutters; far across the plains below, dust rises from approaching imperial cavalry.

books.title: सिंह सेनापति
books.author: राहुल सांकृत्यायन
books.palette: terracotta red, ochre, olive green, warm afternoon light
books.concept: Vaishali, the Licchavi republic, about 500 BCE, from Rahul Sankrityayan's Singh Senapati: General Simha — a tall, broad-shouldered commander in his thirties with a short beard — in ancient Indian battle dress: a quilted cotton armour vest over a white dhoti, a cloth headband, copper armlets on bare arms and a straight iron sword at his hip (no Roman or Greek armour); he stands in a terracotta-walled courtyard beside Rohini, a spirited young woman of the republic in a simple ochre garment; behind them citizens gather on the steps of a pillared wooden assembly hall in warm late-afternoon light.
books.note: Second render: ancient Indian battle dress (quilted cotton vest, dhoti, headband), no Roman armour.

books.title: विस्मृत यात्री
books.author: राहुल सांकृत्यायन
books.palette: glacial blue, snow white, ochre robe
books.concept: The Pamir mountains in the 6th century, from Rahul Sankrityayan's Vismrit Yatri: the Indian Buddhist monk Narendrayash — lean, shaven-headed, in a weathered ochre robe, with a wooden staff and a bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied to his back — walks a narrow snowy mountain pass beside a small Silk Road caravan of Bactrian camels and fur-clad traders; icy wind, a stone cairn at the edge of the path.

books.title: मधुर स्वप्न
books.author: राहुल सांकृत्यायन
books.palette: turquoise tiles, pomegranate red, dusk indigo, firelight
books.concept: The Sasanian Persian empire in the 6th century, from Rahul Sankrityayan's Madhur Swapna: at dusk in a turquoise-tiled courtyard of a mud-brick Persian town, the wandering hero Shaktavat — a bearded young man in a travel-worn tunic and cloak — shares bread with poor farmers and labourers around a fire; behind them, on a lamp-lit palace terrace, richly dressed nobles and robed priests feast; a crescent moon above.

books.title: अँधेरे के जुगनू
books.author: रांगेय राघव
books.palette: deep night blue-black, firefly yellow-green, faint ember
books.concept: An ancient Indian settlement at night, from Rangeya Raghav's Andhere ke Jugnu: outside a fortified wooden town, enslaved labourers in coarse cloth rest by a dying fire after a day of toil; a young enslaved man with an iron cuff on his wrist and a defiant face looks up as fireflies glow around him; behind a palisade, armed guards with spears and an aristocrat in fine robes watch under torchlight.

books.title: चीवर
books.author: रांगेय राघव
books.palette: desert sand, pale gold haze, ochre robe, unbleached white
books.concept: A small Buddhist monastery in the Vindhya forest, early 7th century CE, from Rangeya Raghav's Cheevar: the young widowed princess Rajyashri — in her early twenties, pale and grief-worn, in a plain unbleached white widow's garment, no jewellery, hair loose — stands on the worn brick steps of the vihara, holding out both hands to receive a folded ochre monk's robe from an elderly shaven-headed Buddhist monk in ochre; beside her, her brother King Harshavardhana — youthful, clean-shaven, in white silk with a pearl necklace and a gold armlet — gently touches her wrist, pleading with her to stay; sal trees, a small whitewashed stupa and hazy golden dust in late-morning light.

books.title: पक्षी और आकाश
books.author: रांगेय राघव
books.palette: clear sky blue, white clouds, whitewashed walls, white pigeons
books.concept: An old crowded family haveli in a north Indian town, 1950s, from Rangeya Raghav's Pakshi aur Akash: Dhankumar — a quiet, thoughtful man in his early thirties in a crumpled white kurta-pyjama — stands alone at the parapet of the sunlit rooftop terrace, looking up as a flock of white pigeons bursts into a vast clear sky; a few steps behind him, at the head of the stairs, his two elder brothers in dhoti and kurta glare at him, one clutching a ring of iron keys, the other pointing at him accusingly; washing lines, clay pots and neighbouring rooftops around them in bright morning light.

books.title: प्रतिदान
books.author: रांगेय राघव
books.palette: rust red dust, dusty brown, low red sun
books.concept: The dusty courtyard of Drona's ashram near Hastinapur, Mahabharata era, from Rangeya Raghav's Pratidan: Dronacharya — a lean, grey-bearded Brahmin teacher in his fifties, in a coarse white dhoti and shawl with a sacred thread, a longbow in his hand, his face stern and unsmiling — stands over King Drupada of Panchala, a proud bearded king in torn royal silks and gold ornaments, kneeling in the dust with his wrists tied by a rope; the young prince Arjuna — youthful, clean-shaven, in a warrior's dhoti with a bow and quiver — stands guard beside them; other young princes and a wooden chariot wait behind in drifting dust under a low red sun.

books.title: टूटे काँटे
books.author: वृंदावनलाल वर्मा
books.palette: plum shadows, rose gold, candlelight, amber smoke
books.concept: A lamp-lit Mughal haveli in Delhi, 1739, from Vrindavanlal Verma's Toote Kaante: Nurbai — a celebrated dancer in her twenties, in a flowing plum-and-rose silk anarkali with gold borders, a sheer dupatta and ghungroo bells at her ankles — pauses mid-turn beneath a cusped marble arch, looking back over her shoulder; beside a pillar stands Mohanlal, a sturdy young Jat villager in a plain white pagri and coarse kurta with a bamboo lathi, watching her with quiet longing; through the arches behind them, smoke from the burning city drifts across an amber evening sky.

books.title: भुवन विक्रम
books.author: वृंदावनलाल वर्मा
books.palette: mint green riverbank, white garments, soft morning daylight
books.concept: A hermitage on the banks of the Sarayu near Ayodhya in the later Vedic age, from Vrindavanlal Verma's Bhuvan Vikram: Prince Bhuvan — youthful, clean-shaven, in his early twenties, in an unstitched white garment with a saffron sash, a plain gold armband and a bow over his shoulder — sits humbly on a reed mat beside a small brick fire altar, learning restraint; Gauri — a graceful young woman in a simple pale cotton garment with jasmine in her braid — stands nearby holding a brass water pot, watching him with a gentle, steady gaze; thatched huts, grazing white cows and the misty river behind them in soft morning light.

books.title: गोली
books.author: आचार्य चतुरसेन शास्त्री
books.palette: deep maroon, old gold, lamplight
books.concept: A Rajput palace in Rajasthan, early 20th century, from Acharya Chatursen's Goli: Champa — a beautiful palace maid in her early twenties, in a deep maroon-and-gold bandhani ghagra-choli with a veil drawn over her hair and heavy silver anklets — stands by a carved sandstone jharokha window in a lamp-lit palace hall, glancing back over her shoulder with sad, resigned eyes; across the hall, half in shadow by a pillar, Kisun — a young palace servant in a white angarkha and a red safa turban — waits with lowered eyes; behind them a richly cushioned royal gaddi with bolsters and a silver hookah glows in the lamplight.

books.title: सह्याद्रि की चट्टानें
books.author: आचार्य चतुरसेन शास्त्री
books.palette: midnight blue, silver moonlight, black basalt
books.concept: The night assault on Kondhana fort in the Sahyadri hills, February 1670, from Acharya Chatursen's Sahyadri ki Chattanen: Tanaji Malusare — a powerfully built Maratha commander in his forties with a thick curled moustache, in a saffron pheta turban and a white angarkha with a waist sash, a sword at his hip and a round leather shield on his back — climbs a sheer black basalt cliff on a rope, looking up with fierce resolve, while a line of barefoot Mavla soldiers in dhotis and turbans follows him up the rock; the dark ramparts of the hill fort are faint high above under a moonlit sky, and mist fills the valley below.

books.title: चाणक्य
books.author: भगवतीचरण वर्मा
books.palette: bottle green, brass, oil-lamp light
books.concept: The royal court of Pataliputra, Magadha, 4th century BCE, from Bhagwati Charan Verma's Chanakya: Acharya Vishnugupta — a lean, dark-complexioned Brahmin scholar in his forties, clean-shaven, with a shaven head and a single long tuft of hair that he has just untied, in a plain white dhoti and shawl with a sacred thread — stands defiant in the middle of the hall, eyes blazing, as two palace guards in ancient Indian dress (bare-chested, white dhotis, turbans, spears) seize his arms; behind him, on a raised gilded throne, King Dhana Nanda — a heavy, bejewelled king in silks — laughs scornfully among his courtiers; polished stone pillars, brass oil lamps and bottle-green silk hangings.

books.title: अंधेर नगरी
books.author: भारतेंदु हरिश्चंद्र
books.palette: lemon yellow, fresh white, bright midday sun
books.concept: A bustling bazaar of a mythical north Indian town, from Bharatendu Harishchandra's farce Andher Nagari: the plump young disciple Gobardhandas — round-faced and grinning, with a shaven head and a small tuft, in a saffron dhoti — gorges on sweets from a heaped brass tray at a stall where vegetables and sweets are piled high at one same price; behind him his guru, a lean old Mahant with matted grey hair, rudraksha beads and a saffron robe, raises a warning finger; in the background the foolish king, pompous in an oversized jewelled crown and gaudy silks, is carried through the crowd on a palanquin; plain cloth awnings, no signboards, bright midday sun.

books.title: भारत दुर्दशा
books.author: भारतेंदु हरिश्चंद्र
books.palette: smoky grey, cold blue, a single shaft of warm light
books.concept: An allegorical scene staged like a period film, 1870s colonial India, from Bharatendu Harishchandra's play Bharat Durdasha: Bharat, a frail old man in torn, faded clothes with a broken half-crown on his head and a walking stick beside him, lies unconscious on the cracked stone steps of a ruined ancient temple; Bharat-Bhagya, a grave young man in saffron with a marigold garland, kneels beside him and shakes his shoulder to wake him; in the shadows of the broken pillars behind them a stern colonial official in a black Victorian frock coat walks away with a heavy sack of coins; weeds, dust and one shaft of warm light.

books.title: चाँद का मुँह टेढ़ा है
books.author: गजानन माधव मुक्तिबोध
books.palette: sodium-yellow streetlight, black night, haze
books.concept: A narrow lane in a sleeping Indian industrial town at midnight, 1950s, from Gajanan Madhav Muktibodh's poems Chand ka Munh Tedha Hai: a thin, intense poet in his forties with sunken cheeks, in a crumpled kurta and an old shawl, a beedi between his fingers, stands under a single flickering street lamp and looks up uneasily at a lopsided, crooked crescent moon hanging low over factory chimneys and crumbling tenements; long distorted shadows stretch along the wet cobblestones; a stray dog and a shuttered tea stall.
books.note: Retouched: the crescent moon sat hidden behind the title; it was moved into the free sky right of the first title line and tilted.

books.title: कविता के बहाने
books.author: कुँवर नारायण
books.palette: blush pink, cream, soft morning sunlight
books.concept: A sunlit old Lucknow neighbourhood of joined courtyard houses, from Kunwar Narayan's poem Kavita ke Bahane: a barefoot six-year-old girl in a faded pink cotton frock laughs as she runs across the shared courtyard between two old houses, arms out, chasing a sparrow that flits from one house's window to the other's; bougainvillea and jasmine spill over the low wall; on the veranda an elderly poet in a white kurta and round spectacles sits in a cane chair, smiling as he watches her; soft, warm morning sunlight.
books.note: topAlpha 0.76: stronger light wash so the author line reads over the busy facade.

books.title: नए इलाके में
books.author: अरुण कमल
books.palette: powder blue, white, raw brick, morning light
books.concept: A half-built new neighbourhood on the edge of an Indian city, 1990s, from Arun Kamal's poem Naye Ilake Mein: a middle-aged man with a greying moustache, in a half-sleeve shirt and trousers with a cloth bag on his shoulder, stands lost at a dusty lane corner, looking around in bewilderment; rows of unfinished brick houses with steel rods sticking out of their roofs, bamboo scaffolding, heaps of sand and bricks, and a lone stump where an old peepal tree once stood; he raises his hand hesitantly to knock on a freshly painted iron gate; plain walls, no signboards, bright morning light.

books.title: कलम का सिपाही
books.author: अमृत राय
books.palette: deep teal, brass, lantern amber
books.concept: Banaras, early 1930s, from Amrit Rai's Kalam ka Sipahi, the life of Munshi Premchand: Premchand — a slim man in his fifties with a thick bushy moustache, in a simple khadi kurta and dhoti — sits cross-legged on a floor mat at a low wooden writing desk late at night, writing with a dip pen by the light of a hurricane lantern, the page hidden under his hand; his wife Shivrani Devi, in a plain cotton sari with its end over her head, stands in the doorway holding a cup of tea, watching him with quiet concern; bare lime-washed walls and a small barred window with the night outside.
books.note: Retouched: letter-like scribbles on the page softened.

books.title: खंजन नयन
books.author: अमृतलाल नागर
books.palette: apricot dawn, cream mist, river silver
books.concept: A ghat on the Yamuna in Braj, early 16th century, from Amritlal Nagar's Khanjan Nayan, a novel of the poet Surdas: Surdas — a lean blind singer in his forties with closed, sightless eyes, a short greying beard and a sandalwood tilak, in a white dhoti and shawl — sits on the wet stone steps at dawn, singing with his head tilted up as he plays a tanpura; village women in Braj ghagras with brass pots and a few young cowherd boys stop to listen, enthralled; two small wagtail birds hop on the steps beside him; mist over the river and distant temple spires.

books.title: देशद्रोही
books.author: यशपाल
books.palette: deep indigo dusk, lamp amber
books.concept: Lucknow, 1942, from Yashpal's Deshdrohi: Dr. Bhagwan Das Khanna — a gaunt man in his late thirties with a short beard and tired, burning eyes, in a worn overcoat — stands at the foot of a bungalow's veranda steps at dusk; on the lamp-lit veranda above him Badri Babu, a portly Congress leader in a khadi kurta and Gandhi cap, faces him with suspicion, while Raj, a dignified woman in her thirties in a white khadi sari, stands between them, torn; a bicycle leans against the gate and protesters' torches glow faintly in the street behind.

books.title: अ ट्रैम्प अब्रॉड
books.author: मार्क ट्वेन
books.palette: sage green meadows, linen white, pale alpine sky
books.concept: The Swiss Alps below the Matterhorn, 1878, from Mark Twain's A Tramp Abroad: the author — a man in his early forties with bushy auburn hair and a thick drooping moustache, in a rumpled dark travelling suit and a broad felt hat, an alpenstock in hand — proudly leads an absurdly large expedition of roped-together mountain guides, porters and mules piled with luggage up a gentle grassy slope; beside him his companion Harris, a lanky man in a tweed suit, trudges along under an umbrella; cows graze nearby, unbothered, and snowy peaks rise beyond in clear daylight.

books.title: अंग्रेज़ी उपन्यास और उसके विकास का सिद्धांत
books.author: सिडनी लेनियर
books.palette: sepia brown, old gold, gaslight
books.concept: A lecture room at Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, 1881, from Sidney Lanier's The English Novel and the Principle of Its Development: the poet-critic Sidney Lanier — a frail, thin man in his late thirties with a long dark beard and gentle deep-set eyes, in a black frock coat — lectures from a wooden lectern with one hand raised; a silver flute rests on the table beside a stack of leather-bound books with plain spines; a small audience of men and women in 1880s dress listens intently in the warm gaslight; dark wood panelling and tall windows with winter dusk outside.

books.title: अंग्रेज़ी उपन्यास का विकास
books.author: विलबर एल. क्रॉस
books.palette: seafoam green panelled walls, pale sand, soft daylight
books.concept: A Georgian circulating library in Bath, about 1800, from Wilbur L. Cross's The Development of the English Novel: a young woman in a white muslin Regency gown and a straw bonnet stands by a tall sash window, utterly absorbed in a small leather-bound novel, while behind her two gentlemen in tailcoats and an elderly lady in a lace cap browse long mahogany shelves of leather-bound books with plain spines, and a young clerk carries a stack of volumes; pale seafoam-green panelled walls, soft daylight through the window.

books.title: अंग्रेज़ी छंद का विज्ञान
books.author: सिडनी लेनियर
books.palette: ivory, warm beige, soft daylight
books.concept: A daylight orchestra rehearsal in Baltimore, 1878, from Sidney Lanier's The Science of English Verse: the poet and flautist Sidney Lanier — a frail, thin man in his mid-thirties with a long dark beard, in a black frock coat — stands among seated musicians playing a silver flute with his eyes closed, while an old conductor lowers his baton and the violinists pause to listen; soft daylight from tall windows, dust in the air, a wooden stage.

books.title: अंग्रेज़ी साहित्य का इतिहास
books.author: हिप्पोलाइट टेन
books.palette: pale lilac dawn, lavender mist, soft white, grey-green sea
books.concept: The English Channel at dawn in the 1860s, from Hippolyte Taine's History of English Literature: the French critic Hippolyte Taine — a man in his thirties with a full dark beard and small round spectacles, in a dark wool overcoat — stands at the rail of a paddle steamer holding a closed notebook, gazing at the white cliffs of Dover rising out of the sea mist; a few Victorian passengers in top hats, bonnets and shawls stand along the deck behind him; gulls overhead, soft pale-lilac dawn light over grey-green water.

books.title: अपराध और प्रथा आदिम समाज में
books.author: ब्रोनिस्लाव मालिनोव्स्की
books.palette: aqua lagoon, white coral sand, bright midday light
books.concept: The Trobriand Islands, about 1916, from Bronisław Malinowski's study of law, custom and reciprocity there: on a white coral beach beside an aqua lagoon, men of a Trobriand village in traditional fibre waistcloths, with shell armbands and red shell-disc necklaces, ceremonially present a decorated shell necklace to visitors who have just landed in a large outrigger canoe with a carved, painted prow; a dignified elder looks on; at the edge of the scene the young anthropologist Malinowski — balding, in round spectacles and white tropical clothes — watches respectfully with a notebook in hand; palm trees and bright midday light.

books.title: आज कत्ल हो के रहेगा
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: petrol blue night, amber lamplight
books.concept: A 1970s Delhi bungalow at night, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Aaj Katl Ho Ke Rahega: a frightened, wealthy businessman in his fifties in a silk dressing gown stands rigid by a heavy curtained window, staring at a tall pendulum clock with a plain dial whose hands are nearing midnight; across the room a hard-eyed private detective in his thirties with a thick moustache, in a brown leather jacket, checks his wristwatch, a revolver holstered at his side; a black rotary telephone lies off its hook on the table; deep blue night beyond the window, amber lamplight.

books.title: आस्तीन के सांप
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: red nightclub light, black shadows, cigarette smoke, cyan glints
books.concept: A crowded 1970s Bombay nightclub, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Aasteen ke Saanp: two old friends in their forties embrace warmly beside a table of whisky glasses — one in a white safari suit beaming trustingly, the other in a dark suit smiling over his friend's shoulder with cold eyes while his free hand, hidden behind his friend's back, holds a small revolver; a cabaret singer in a sequinned sari is blurred in the background; red light and drifting cigarette smoke.

books.title: इश्तिहारी मुजरिम
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: khaki dust, faded cotton, pale hazy sky
books.concept: A crowded north Indian railway platform on a hazy summer morning in the 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Ishtihari Mujrim: a hunted man in his thirties with a few days' stubble, in a crumpled shirt with a cloth bag and a cap pulled low, stands among jostling passengers and red-shirted porters, glancing over his shoulder at two policemen in khaki uniforms who are comparing a small photograph with faces in the crowd; a steam locomotive breathes white clouds behind them; dust in the air.
books.note: topAlpha 0.84: stronger light wash so the author line reads over the dark locomotive.

books.title: कालगर्ल की हत्या
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: wine-red carpet, dim gold light, deep shadow
books.concept: A dim corridor of a 1970s Delhi hotel late at night, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Callgirl ki Hatya: a sharp, sardonic investigative journalist in his thirties in a tweed jacket, a cigarette in his fingers, and a tired police inspector in khaki crouch beside an open door that spills yellow light onto the wine-red carpet, studying a single red high-heeled sandal and a scattered string of broken beads; a frightened young bellboy in uniform watches from down the hall; no body is visible.

books.title: काला मोती
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: aubergine purple shadows, dull gold lamplight
books.concept: A private card room in a 1970s Bombay hotel suite, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Kala Moti: a coolly glamorous woman in a black chiffon sari, a single large black pearl on a fine chain at her throat, sits at a baize card table watching through cigarette smoke as an elderly jeweller with a loupe examines another black pearl under a lamp; a sweating man in a white dinner jacket leans in greedily, and in the shadows behind them a gloved hand rests on the back of a chair; deep purple shadows, dull gold lamplight.

books.title: खतरनाक अपराधी
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: oxblood red, black, tarnished brass lamplight
books.concept: A dim godown office by the Bombay docks at night in the 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Khatarnak Apradhi: a calm, sharply dressed criminal mastermind in his forties with a salt-and-pepper beard and a thin scar on his cheek, in a dark suit, sits at a desk moving a piece on a chessboard, his cold eyes on the viewer, while two nervous henchmen stand behind him; through a grimy window the red beacon of a police jeep flickers across stacked wooden crates; a tarnished brass lamp.

books.title: खतरनाक ब्लैकमेलर
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: slate grey dusk, deep teal, one warm lamp
books.concept: Lodhi Garden in Delhi at dusk, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Khatarnak Blackmailer: a smug blackmailer in his forties in a cream safari suit and tinted glasses lounges on a park bench, holding up a few photographs with their backs to the camera, while a respectable, sweating businessman in a grey suit hands him a fat brown envelope with trembling fingers; old domed tombs and dark trees behind them, a single park lamp just switching on.

books.title: दौलत और खून
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: royal crimson, deep shadow, warm gold lamplight
books.concept: The panelled study of a Bombay mansion at night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Daulat aur Khoon: a powerful grey-haired industrialist in a silk kurta sits behind a heavy desk with open steel cash boxes, watching coldly as a slick politician in a white Nehru jacket and a scarred gangster in a leather jacket shake hands across the desk; heavy crimson curtains, a brass desk lamp, cigar smoke.

books.title: पुराने गुनाह नये गुनाहगार
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: charcoal, smoky grey, rain, lantern amber
books.concept: A rainy night in an old Delhi bungalow, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Purane Gunah Naye Gunahgar: a respectable retired gentleman in his sixties, in a cardigan and spectacles, stands frozen in his dim study holding an old black-and-white photograph (seen from behind) that has just arrived in a torn envelope; through the rain-streaked window behind him a young stranger in a leather jacket watches from beneath a streetlamp.

books.title: पैंसठ लाख की डकैती
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: storm steel blue, black rain, gold lantern light
books.concept: A hideout in an abandoned textile mill on a stormy night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Painsath Lakh ki Dakaiti: four tense robbers in 1970s shirts and bell-bottoms crouch around a hurricane lantern and three battered steel trunks; while two of them stare at the open loot, a lean, moustached man at the edge quietly slides his hand toward a revolver tucked in his belt, and the gang leader notices; rain lashing through broken windows.

books.title: बदसूरत चेहरे
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: burnished copper bulbs, deep shadow
books.concept: A backstage make-up room of an old Bombay theatre at night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Badsurat Chehre: a man sits before a bulb-lit mirror peeling a grotesque latex disguise from his face, half of it still on, revealing a handsome face beneath; in the mirror, a woman in a dark sari watches him from the doorway with suspicion; wigs, greasepaint pots and costumes hang around him in warm copper light.

books.title: बैंक वैन रॉबरी
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: desert sand, dust, pale hazy sky
books.concept: A dusty highway outside a north Indian town in hard noon light, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Bank Van Robbery: an armoured bank van is blocked by a truck parked across the road; four robbers in bell-bottoms with cloth masks over their faces haul out steel cash boxes while the uniformed guard stands with raised hands; one robber pauses to glance suspiciously at his partners; dust swirling in the air.

books.title: ब्लैकमेलर की हत्या
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: ink-black night, ember orange glow
books.concept: A ransacked 1970s Bombay apartment at night, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Blackmailer ki Hatya: a police inspector in khaki holds up a strip of photo negatives against his torch beam, studying it, while a nervous young woman in a sari and an older man in a cardigan stand pressed against the wall; an overturned chair, a smashed camera and an open, emptied wall safe; no body is visible.

books.title: मीना मर्डर केस
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: pearl-white daylight, pale gold, whitewashed walls
books.concept: A crowded 1970s Delhi sessions courtroom on a bright day, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Meena Murder Case: a sharp defence lawyer in a black coat and white bands points at a sweating witness in the box, while the young accused man stands tense in the dock and the grey-haired judge leans forward on the high bench; ceiling fans, tall windows with pale daylight, spectators on wooden benches.

books.title: मूर्ति की चोरी
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: warm cream stone, marigold orange, morning light
books.concept: An ancient stone temple in a south Indian village at morning, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Murti ki Chori: in the sanctum doorway an elderly priest kneels in shock beside an empty stone pedestal strewn with fallen marigold garlands, where a bronze idol once stood; a police inspector in khaki examines a broken iron lock, villagers crowd behind, and at the edge of the scene a suspicious antique dealer in a linen suit watches quietly.

books.title: मौत का खेल
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: card-table baize green, cigarette smoke, one amber bulb
books.concept: An illegal gambling den in a Bombay basement at night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Maut ka Khel: a desperate young man in a sweat-soaked shirt sits at a green baize card table facing a cold, heavy-set gang boss with gold rings; between them lie a fanned deck of plain-backed cards, a pile of cash and a revolver pointing at nobody; hard-faced onlookers lean in through thick cigarette smoke under one swinging amber bulb.

books.title: रिपोर्टर की हत्या
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: gunmetal grey, cold steel, one yellow work-lamp
books.concept: A newspaper press hall in Delhi past midnight, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Reporter ki Hatya: a young crime reporter in a sweater vest and loosened tie clutches a manila envelope to his chest and glances back in fear between giant steel rotary presses rolling blank white paper, while two thugs in raincoats step out of the shadows behind him; an old ink-stained press worker freezes; cold steel light and one yellow work-lamp.

books.title: रेड सर्किल सोसाइटी
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: scarlet red, black shadow, candle gold
books.concept: A cellar beneath an old Bombay mansion at night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Red Circle Society: eight members of a secret society in dark suits and plain black eye-masks sit around a round table draped in scarlet cloth, a large plain red circle painted on the stone floor around them, candles burning; their silver-haired leader raises a hand to speak, while a young journalist hides behind a stone pillar in the foreground, watching.

books.title: विक्षिप्त हत्यारा
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: sickly absinthe green, flickering tube-light, deep shadow
books.concept: A police lock-up interrogation room in Delhi at night, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Vikshipt Hatyara: a thin, unshaven man with wild eyes sits handcuffed on a steel chair, rocking slightly and smiling at his own reflection in a cracked mirror, while a calm police psychiatrist in spectacles and a grim inspector watch him from behind a barred window; a flickering green-white tube-light, peeling walls.

books.title: शैतान की मौत
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: ochre earth, dusty gold evening sky
books.concept: The Chambal ravines at dusky evening, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Shaitan ki Maut: a feared bandit chief's riderless horse stands on a ridge of eroded earth beside his dropped rifle and fallen red turban, while a young avenger in a dusty kurta lowers his own rifle, breathing hard, and a police party in khaki climbs up the slope behind him; dust hanging in golden light.

books.title: समुद्र में खून
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: ultramarine sea at dusk, white deck lamps, storm clouds
books.concept: A small coastal steamer alone on the Arabian Sea at stormy dusk, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Samudra mein Khoon: on the rain-wet deck the grey-bearded captain in a white cap, a nervous young couple, a burly cook and a lean sailor with a torn sleeve stand in a tense circle by a coil of rope and a plain white lifebuoy, each watching the others with suspicion; no land in sight, white deck lamps, dark waves.

books.title: हत्या की रात
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: moonstone blue-grey night, white torch beams
books.concept: A narrow old Delhi lane at two in the morning during a power cut, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Hatya ki Raat: a police inspector and a constable run with torches toward an old haveli whose single upstairs window glows, while a frightened elderly chowkidar with a lathi and a hurricane lantern points the way; cobblestones wet with dew, moonlight, a stray dog watching.

books.title: हत्यारे
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: eucalyptus grey-green, misty white morning
books.concept: The drawing room of a hill-station bungalow in Mussoorie on a misty morning, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Hatyare: six suspects — a widow in a white sari, a playboy son in a cravat, a family doctor with a bag, a bespectacled secretary, an old servant and a mysterious guest in a tweed coat — sit and stand around the room, each glancing at someone else, while a detective in a trench coat watches them from beside the stone fireplace; misty light through tall windows.

books.title: हांगकांग में हंगामा
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: jade-green harbour water, hazy morning sky
books.concept: Aberdeen Harbour in Hong Kong on a hazy morning, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Hongkong mein Hungama: a lean Indian agent in a light linen suit leaps from one wooden sampan to the next across the crowded floating village, while two armed men chase him in a speedboat and an old boatwoman ducks; junk boats and green hills in the haze, jade-green water.

books.title: होटल में खून
books.author: Surender Mohan Pathak
books.palette: champagne gold, cream marble, morning light
books.concept: The Art Deco lobby of a grand Bombay hotel in morning light, 1970s, from Surender Mohan Pathak's crime thriller Hotel mein Khoon: a police inspector with a notebook questions the guests held in the lobby — a cabaret dancer in a sequined gown under a shawl, a sweating businessman, a foreign tourist couple, a nervous bellboy and the manager in a tailcoat — while constables guard the revolving door and a grand curved staircase rises behind them; cream marble and brass.

books.title: अपने कत्ल की सुपारी
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: cobalt-blue night, wet reflections, one red neon glow
books.concept: A dim Irani café booth in Bombay on a rainy night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Apne Katl ki Supari: a calm, well-dressed man in his thirties slides a thick envelope of cash across the marble table to a scarred contract killer in a leather jacket; between them lies a small black-and-white photograph showing the client's own face, and the killer stares from the photo to the man in disbelief; rain on the window, cobalt night outside, one red neon glow.
books.note: Retouched: the café window neon read IRANI CAFÉ; softened to an out-of-focus red glow with an elliptical feathered blur (original kept in cover-art-raw/_orig).

books.title: असली खिलाड़ी
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: polished walnut wood, brass lamp, deep brown shadow
books.concept: The study of a Bombay underworld mansion at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Asli Khiladi: a cool young man in a leather jacket moves a knight on a wooden chessboard against a silver-haired don with a walking cane, who leans back with a thin smile; two henchmen stand behind the don and a nervous woman in a silk sari watches from the door; polished walnut panelling, a brass lamp over the board.

books.title: एक मुट्ठी दर्द
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: pale mauve dawn, soft grey, washed walls
books.concept: Dawn in a Bombay chawl, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Ek Mutthi Dard: a grief-stricken young man sits on worn stone steps with a broken red glass bangle clenched in his tight fist, his eyes red and jaw set, while his old mother weeps in the doorway behind him and a neighbour lowers his head; at the far end of the lane a police jeep waits in the pale mauve light, washing hanging from balconies.

books.title: कलयुग की रामायण
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: rani-pink and magenta festival lights, black night
books.concept: A neighbourhood Ramlila in Delhi at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Kalyug ki Ramayan: on the bright stage, actors costumed as Ram and Ravan face each other with bows; in the front row a garlanded local don in a white kurta sits as chief guest, smiling, flanked by henchmen with guns under their shawls, while an honest young police inspector in plain clothes watches him from the standing crowd; strings of pink and magenta festival bulbs.

books.title: कानून का बेटा
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: buttercream walls, warm morning sun, khaki
books.concept: A modest Delhi home at sunrise, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Kanoon ka Beta: a young police officer in a crisp new khaki uniform stands before a garlanded framed portrait of his late father, a police inspector, while his widowed mother in a white sari puts a red tilak on his forehead with her thumb and his little sister holds his peaked cap; warm morning sun on buttercream walls.

books.title: कानून बदल डालो
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: violet dusk sky, sodium lamps, smoke
books.concept: Outside a Delhi district court at dusk, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Kanoon Badal Daalo: an angry crowd of common people — mill workers, students, a widow holding a child — surrounds a young lawyer in a black coat standing on a parked jeep with his fist raised, while a line of riot police with cane shields and lathis holds them back; plain cloth banners without any writing, smoke drifting under sodium lamps, violet sky.

books.title: केशव पंडित
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: parchment cream, warm wood, daylight
books.concept: A crowded Indian courtroom by day, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's novel Keshav Pandit: Keshav Pandit — a sharp-eyed young man in a crisp white kurta and shawl, with a calm half-smile — stands in the aisle holding a thick law book under his arm, while behind him a powerful gangster in a safari suit and a corrupt police officer glare at him and the lawyers turn to look; warm wooden benches, parchment-coloured daylight from tall windows.

books.title: खलीफा
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: tobacco brown, gold rings, tungsten light
books.concept: A dim Bombay dockside warehouse at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Khalifa: the underworld boss called Khalifa — a heavy-set silver-haired man in a black silk shirt with gold rings — sits on a carved wooden chair among crates while gang members bow to touch his feet and a frightened shopkeeper waits with folded hands; a single tungsten lamp, cigarette smoke, tobacco-brown shadows.

books.title: चकमा
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: pewter grey, hazy daylight, steam
books.concept: A crowded Bombay railway terminus platform at rush hour, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Chakma: in the pushing crowd beside a steaming train, a quick-handed con man in a disguise of spectacles and a false moustache swaps an identical leather briefcase with a gangster's courier who is looking the other way, while a plain-clothes police informer notices from behind a pillar; hazy daylight through the station roof, porters in red shirts.
books.note: Retouched: the locomotive buffer beam carried two small WDM-2 markings; softened with small elliptical feathered blurs (original kept in cover-art-raw/_orig).

books.title: तीन तिलंगे
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: tangerine and lemon street colours, bright noon
books.concept: A busy Bombay market street at bright noon, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Teen Tilange: three mischievous young friends — one tall in a leather jacket, one chubby in a loud printed shirt, one skinny with big glasses — run laughing toward the camera with a stolen suitcase, while three angry goons chase them and a fruit cart overturns, oranges rolling across the road; colourful shop awnings without any writing.

books.title: फांसी दो कानून को
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: graphite grey, cold moonlight, rope brown
books.concept: An empty Indian courtroom at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Faansi Do Kanoon Ko: a hangman's rope noose hangs from a ceiling beam right in front of a tall blindfolded statue of Justice holding scales, while a grim young man in a dark shawl, disillusioned and furious, stands beside it with his fists clenched and an elderly judge in black robes stares in shock from the doorway; cold moonlight through high windows across empty wooden benches.

books.title: वर्दी वाला गुंडा
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: mustard yellow, khaki, hot white noon
books.concept: A crowded Delhi vegetable market at hot noon, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Vardi Wala Gunda: a swaggering corrupt police inspector in khaki with aviator sunglasses and a swagger stick pockets a fold of cash from a frightened old vendor, while a gangster in a printed shirt leans on a police jeep laughing and onlookers look away; baskets of tomatoes and chillies, harsh white sunlight.
books.note: Retouched: the police jeep carried DELHI POLICE lettering and a DL 1C 4532 number plate; both softened with elliptical feathered blurs (original in cover-art-raw/_orig). topAlpha 0.8 so the author reads over the busy market.

books.title: विजय और विकास
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: electric-blue night, city lights below
books.concept: A rooftop water tank above a Delhi neighbourhood at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Vijay aur Vikas: Vijay — a witty secret agent in his thirties in a sports jacket, grinning, pistol in hand — and Vikas — a fearless, athletic teenage boy with sharp eyes — crouch back to back, the boy pointing down at a smugglers' van in the lane below; city lights spread out under an electric-blue night sky.

books.title: सबसे बड़ी मर्डर मिस्ट्री
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: mahogany wood, crystal sparkle, flashbulb white
books.concept: The grand staircase hall of a maharaja's palace at night, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Sabse Badi Murder Mystery: a famous detective in a white suit stands halfway up the stairs addressing a crowd of suspects — a prince in a sherwani, a film actress, an army general, a butler and maids — while a huge crystal chandelier lies shattered on the marble floor in the centre and press photographers' flashbulbs pop at the doorway; mahogany panelling, crystal sparkle.

books.title: हिंद का बेटा
books.author: Ved Prakash Sharma
books.palette: pink-gold dawn on snow, deep blue shadows
books.concept: A snowy Himalayan border pass at dawn, 1980s, from Ved Prakash Sharma's thriller Hind ka Beta: a young Indian army commando in snow camouflage, rifle slung, marches three captured smugglers with their hands raised across the snow, their mule loaded with contraband crates behind them, while his comrades cover him from the rocks; the peaks glow pink and gold, deep blue shadows on the snow.

books.title: इंसाफ का जनाजा
books.author: Ved Prakash Kamboj
books.palette: ash grey dust, white cloth, overcast light
books.concept: A dusty north Indian town street under an overcast sky, from Ved Prakash Kamboj's crime thriller Insaaf ka Janaza: a silent protest procession carries a bamboo bier draped in white cloth on which lie a pair of brass scales of justice and a closed black law book, as if in a funeral; a defiant old schoolteacher with a white beard leads the mourners, villagers follow with bowed heads, and a line of police watches uneasily from beside a jeep.
books.note: topAlpha 0.8 so the author reads over the crowded street.

books.title: कदम कदम पर धोखा
books.author: Ved Prakash Kamboj
books.palette: quicksilver mirror reflections, cold cyan light
books.concept: The hall of mirrors at a deserted funfair at night, 1970s, from Ved Prakash Kamboj's spy thriller Kadam Kadam par Dhokha: a sharp Indian secret agent in a dark suit and a beautiful double agent in a black sari face each other among dozens of their own reflections, both aiming revolvers at the wrong reflection, neither sure which figure is real; cold cyan light glinting off endless mirrors.

books.title: खतरे की खोपड़ी
books.author: Ved Prakash Kamboj
books.palette: sulphur-yellow torchlight, black rock
books.concept: A hidden cave hideout in the hills at night, 1970s, from Ved Prakash Kamboj's thriller Khatre ki Khopdi: a detective in a safari suit and his young assistant creep in with a flaming torch through an entrance carved into a gigantic stone skull, its eye sockets dark, while masked gang members with rifles stand guard deeper inside around crates; bats overhead, sulphur-yellow torchlight on black rock.

books.title: प्रेतों का निर्माता
books.author: Ved Prakash Kamboj
books.palette: verdigris green-blue, white projector beam
books.concept: A secret cellar laboratory beneath a haunted haveli at night, 1970s, from Ved Prakash Kamboj's mystery Preton ka Nirmata: a wild-haired scientist in a stained lab coat operates an old film projector and a smoke machine that throw ghostly white human shapes onto hanging muslin sheets, while a detective peers in through a gap in a broken wall, discovering the trick; glass jars, coils of wire, verdigris-green walls.

books.title: रेलगाड़ी का भूत
books.author: Ved Prakash Kamboj
books.palette: white fog lit by a headlight, cold blue edges
books.concept: A lonely railway halt in north India on a foggy winter night, 1970s, from Ved Prakash Kamboj's mystery Railgadi ka Bhoot: the headlight of an approaching steam locomotive glows through thick fog, and on the empty track ahead stands a pale figure wrapped in a white shawl, while a sceptical detective with a torch and a terrified old station master holding a lantern watch from the low platform; frosted rails, no signboards.

books.title: एक रात का मेहमान
books.author: Om Prakash Sharma
books.palette: tempest grey-green, lightning white, lantern amber
books.concept: A lonely dak bungalow in the hills on a stormy night, 1970s, from Om Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Ek Raat ka Mehman: an elderly caretaker couple open the creaking door to a drenched stranger in a long raincoat and hat, holding a small leather suitcase, his face half in shadow; the old wife lifts a lantern to see him while the husband grips the door; lightning flashes over the pines behind him.

books.title: एक हसीना थी
books.author: Om Prakash Sharma
books.palette: rose-gold spotlight, smoky black club
books.concept: A smoky 1970s Delhi nightclub, from Om Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Ek Haseena Thi: a beautiful, mysterious singer in a shimmering chiffon sari sings at an old microphone in a rose-gold spotlight, her eyes fixed on one table, while a sharp detective in a dark suit watches her from the bar and a nervous rich man at the front table loosens his collar; cigarette smoke curling through the light.

books.title: कब्रिस्तान का षड्यंत्र
books.author: Om Prakash Sharma
books.palette: moss-green stone, lantern gold, midnight
books.concept: An old colonial cemetery in Delhi at midnight, 1970s, from Om Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Kabristan ka Shadyantra: a detective and his young assistant crouch behind a weathered stone angel, watching three men by lantern light lift a heavy wooden box out of a freshly opened grave pit; mossy tombstones, tangled trees, mist creeping over the ground; no bodies anywhere.

books.title: केसरीगढ़ की काली रात
books.author: Om Prakash Sharma
books.palette: saffron sandstone, black moonless sky, torch fire
books.concept: The gate of a crumbling Rajasthani fort town called Kesarigarh on a black moonless night, 1970s, from Om Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Kesarigarh ki Kaali Raat: a lone detective in a dark coat walks in through the massive saffron sandstone gateway holding up a flaming torch, bats wheeling overhead, while frightened villagers peep from carved jharokha windows and an old guard with a spear backs away; deep shadow beyond the torchlight.

books.title: विषकन्या
books.author: Om Prakash Sharma
books.palette: nightshade purple, emerald silk, candlelight
books.concept: A palace drawing room at night, 1970s, from Om Prakash Sharma's crime thriller Vishkanya: a breathtakingly beautiful woman in an emerald and black silk sari smiles at an infatuated rich old nobleman while, out of his sight, she tilts open a jewelled ring over his crystal glass; behind a velvet curtain a detective watches, unseen; candlelight, nightshade-purple shadows.

books.title: 47 Naatkal
books.author: Sivasankari
books.palette: frosted window white, pale lilac, cold daylight
books.concept: A village outside Paris in winter, early 1980s, from Sivasankari's Tamil novel 47 Naatkal: a young newly married Tamil bride in a silk sari, with jasmine fading in her hair, stands alone at the frosted attic window of a strange French house, holding the curtain, looking out at snow on the slate roofs with frightened, homesick eyes; on the snowy lane below, her husband walks arm in arm with a French woman; cold pale daylight.

books.title: Aa Maratheyum Marannu Marannu Njan
books.author: K. R. Meera
books.palette: wet monsoon green, soft grey sky
books.concept: A rain-soaked courtyard of an old Kerala tharavad house during the monsoon, present day, from K. R. Meera's Malayalam novella Aa Maratheyum Marannu Marannu Njan: a middle-aged woman in a pale cotton sari stands under a huge old tree, one palm pressed to its wet bark and eyes closed as if trying to remember something she forced herself to forget; fallen leaves on wet laterite stones, the tiled house behind her, soft grey light.

books.title: Aa...!
books.author: Sujatha
books.palette: green-blue monitor glow, dark room
books.concept: A small rented flat in Madras late at night, early 1990s, from Sujatha's Tamil thriller Aa...!: a young computer engineer sits bolt upright on his bed clutching his head with both hands, eyes wide in terror as if a voice is speaking inside his head, his face lit by the green-blue glow of an old computer monitor on the desk, while his worried young wife stands frozen in the doorway with her hand at her mouth.
books.note: Retouched: the wall shelf carving looked like pseudo-letters; softened with a small elliptical blur (original in cover-art-raw/_orig). The monitor shows only unreadable code-like lines.

books.title: Aadhalinal Kadhal Seiveer
books.author: Sujatha
books.palette: flamingo-pink dusk sky, sea grey
books.concept: Marina Beach in Madras at dusk, 1980s, from Sujatha's Tamil novel Aadhalinal Kadhal Seiveer: a young couple — a bespectacled young man in a striped shirt and a young woman in a half-sari with jasmine in her long braid — sit close on the sand laughing and sharing a paper cone of roasted peanuts, while in the background her stern elder brother watches them from beside a parked scooter; fishing boats on the shore, flamingo-pink sky.

books.title: Aagamana
books.author: Yaddanapudi Sulochana Rani
books.palette: honey-gold dawn, whitewashed verandah
books.concept: The verandah of a grand old family house in coastal Andhra at dawn, 1970s, from Yaddanapudi Sulochana Rani's Telugu novel Aagamana: a poised young woman in a cotton sari steps down from a horse-drawn cart with a single suitcase, arriving, while a stern grandmother in a white sari waits on the steps and a curious young man in a kurta pauses at a pillar; coconut palms, honey-gold early light.
